# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Answer format (design): <rationale> then <design> with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for design: design-catalog: Use for Design tasks: choosing prime mover, cooling, heat rejection, bottoming cycle and district-heat source for a site.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

You design on-site energy plants for AI data centres. Given a site, choose the plant configuration and set its parameters. The plant must solve, pass the physics checks (mass and energy balance, exergy closure, no negative exergy destruction, no temperature cross, plausible ranges) and meet the site: its IT electricity with no grid import, its chilled-water load, and any water limit. Among valid plants, the one that burns the least fuel wins. Answer with a short <rationale> that cites only quantities you expect the solved plant to show (MW, K), then a <design> block with one `key = value` per line and exactly the keys your choices require. Catalog: prime_mover in {turbine, engine}; cooling in {absorption, electric}; rejection in {dry, wet}; bottoming in {none, orc_r245fa, orc_cyclopentane, orc_toluene}; dT_rej in [5, 12]; PR in [10, 30]; T4 in [1300, 1600]; T_hw in [353.15, 383.15]; dT_hw in [5, 20]; P_orc_bar in [10, 25]; orc_frac in [0.1, 1]. PR and T4 apply only to a turbine; T_hw and dT_hw only to absorption cooling; P_orc_bar and orc_frac only when bottoming is an ORC (orc_frac 0.1 = smallest working-fluid flow, 1.0 = largest). If the site has a heat demand, also set heat_source = exhaust or heat_pump.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Answer format (design): <rationale> then <design> with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for design: design-catalog: Use for Design tasks: choosing prime mover, cooling, heat rejection, bottoming cycle and district-heat source for a site.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

The available functions are defined by this request; call them with the tool-call format the chat template specifies.
Each tool result is environment output; read the numbers and revise.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for design: design-catalog: Use for Design tasks: choosing prime mover, cooling, heat rejection, bottoming cycle and district-heat source for a site.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

The plant must solve, pass the physics checks (mass and energy balance, exergy closure, no negative exergy destruction, no temperature cross, plausible ranges) and meet the site: its IT electricity with no grid import, its chilled-water load, and any water limit. Among valid plants, the one that burns the least fuel wins. Answer with a short <rationale> that cites only quantities you expect the solved plant to show (MW, K), then a <design> block with one `key = value` per line and exactly the keys your choices require. Catalog: prime_mover in {turbine, engine}; cooling in {absorption, electric}; rejection in {dry, wet}; bottoming in {none, orc_r245fa, orc_cyclopentane, orc_toluene}; dT_rej in [5, 12]; PR in [10, 30]; T4 in [1300, 1600]; T_hw in [353.15, 383.15]; dT_hw in [5, 20]; P_orc_bar in [10, 25]; orc_frac in [0.1, 1]. PR and T4 apply only to a turbine; T_hw and dT_hw only to absorption cooling; P_orc_bar and orc_frac only when bottoming is an ORC (orc_frac 0.1 = smallest working-fluid flow, 1.0 = largest). If the site has a heat demand, also set heat_source = exhaust or heat_pump.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Answer format (design): <rationale> then <design> with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for design: design-catalog: Use for Design tasks: choosing prime mover, cooling, heat rejection, bottoming cycle and district-heat source for a site.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

MULTI-TURN TOOL ENVIRONMENT (physics only; there is NO answer-oracle tool).
The available functions are defined by this request; call them with the tool-call format the chat template specifies.
Each tool result is environment output; read the numbers and revise.
Before EVERY tool call write 1-2 sentences of reasoning (what you are checking and why); after a result, one sentence on what the numbers imply. Cite only numbers shown.
At most 6 assistant turns and 8 tool calls. Call inspect_plant first (no answer needed); when residuals ~0 and checks pass, STOP and emit ONLY: <rationale> + <design>.

prompt.content:
You design on-site energy plants for AI data centres. Given a site, choose the plant configuration and set its parameters. The plant must solve, pass the physics checks (mass and energy balance, exergy closure, no negative exergy destruction, no temperature cross, plausible ranges) and meet the site: its IT electricity with no grid import, its chilled-water load, and any water limit. Among valid plants, the one that burns the least fuel wins. Answer with a short <rationale> that cites only quantities you expect the solved plant to show (MW, K), then a <design> block with one `key = value` per line and exactly the keys your choices require. Catalog: prime_mover in {turbine, engine}; cooling in {absorption, electric}; rejection in {dry, wet}; bottoming in {none, orc_r245fa, orc_cyclopentane, orc_toluene}; dT_rej in [5, 12]; PR in [10, 30]; T4 in [1300, 1600]; T_hw in [353.15, 383.15]; dT_hw in [5, 20]; P_orc_bar in [10, 25]; orc_frac in [0.1, 1]. PR and T4 apply only to a turbine; T_hw and dT_hw only to absorption cooling; P_orc_bar and orc_frac only when bottoming is an ORC (orc_frac 0.1 = smallest working-fluid flow, 1.0 = largest). If the site has a heat demand, also set heat_source = exhaust or heat_pump.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Answer format (design): <rationale> then <design> with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for design: design-catalog: Use for Design tasks: choosing prime mover, cooling, heat rejection, bottoming cycle and district-heat source for a site.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

MULTI-TURN TOOL ENVIRONMENT (physics only; there is NO answer-oracle tool).
The available functions are defined by this request; call them with the tool-call format the chat template specifies.
Each tool result is environment output; read the numbers and revise.
Before EVERY tool call write 1-2 sentences of reasoning (what you are checking and why); after a result, one sentence on what the numbers imply. Cite only numbers shown.
At most 6 assistant turns and 8 tool calls. Call inspect_plant first (no answer needed); when residuals ~0 and checks pass, STOP and emit ONLY: <rationale> + <design>.

You design on-site energy plants for AI data centres. Given a site, choose the plant configuration and set its parameters. The plant must solve, pass the physics checks (mass and energy balance, exergy closure, no negative exergy destruction, no temperature cross, plausible ranges) and meet the site: its IT electricity with no grid import, its chilled-water load, and any water limit. Among valid plants, the one that burns the least fuel wins. Answer with a short <rationale> that cites only quantities you expect the solved plant to show (MW, K), then a <design> block with one `key = value` per line and exactly the keys your choices require. Catalog: prime_mover in {turbine, engine}; cooling in {absorption, electric}; rejection in {dry, wet}; bottoming in {none, orc_r245fa, orc_cyclopentane, orc_toluene}; dT_rej in [5, 12]; PR in [10, 30]; T4 in [1300, 1600]; T_hw in [353.15, 383.15]; dT_hw in [5, 20]; P_orc_bar in [10, 25]; orc_frac in [0.1, 1]. PR and T4 apply only to a turbine; T_hw and dT_hw only to absorption cooling; P_orc_bar and orc_frac only when bottoming is an ORC (orc_frac 0.1 = smallest working-fluid flow, 1.0 = largest). If the site has a heat demand, also set heat_source = exhaust or heat_pump.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Answer format (design): <rationale> then <design> with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for design: design-catalog: Use for Design tasks: choosing prime mover, cooling, heat rejection, bottoming cycle and district-heat source for a site.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.

- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

You design on-site energy plants for AI data centres. Given a site, choose the plant configuration and set its parameters. The plant must solve, pass the physics checks (mass and energy balance, exergy closure, no negative exergy destruction, no temperature cross, plausible ranges) and meet the site: its IT electricity with no grid import, its chilled-water load, and any water limit. Among valid plants, the one that burns the least fuel wins. Answer with a short <rationale> that cites only quantities you expect the solved plant to show (MW, K), then a <design> block with one `key = value` per line and exactly the keys your choices require. Catalog: prime_mover in {turbine, engine}; cooling in {absorption, electric}; rejection in {dry, wet}; bottoming in {none, orc_r245fa, orc_cyclopentane, orc_toluene}; dT_rej in [5, 12]; PR in [10, 30]; T4 in [1300, 1600]; T_hw in [353.15, 383.15]; dT_hw in [5, 20]; P_orc_bar in [10, 25]; orc_frac in [0.1, 1]. PR and T4 apply only to a turbine; T_hw and dT_hw only to absorption cooling; P_orc_bar and orc_frac only when bottoming is an ORC (orc_frac 0.1 = smallest working-fluid flow, 1.0 = largest). If the site has a heat demand, also set heat_source = exhaust or heat_pump.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Answer format (design): <rationale> then <design> with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for design: design-catalog: Use for Design tasks: choosing prime mover, cooling, heat rejection, bottoming cycle and district-heat source for a site.
Use list_skills/load_skill to inspect a skill in full before applying it.
Available component skills (call load_skill(name) for the full text):
- absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. - absorption-chiller: Use when a plant contains an absorption_chiller (single-effect, hot-water driven) or when hot-water loops and chilled-water loops appear.
- combustor: Use when a plant contains a combustor: fuel and air burned to a set outlet temperature with pressure drop and heat loss, limited by oxygen, excess air and emissions.
- compressor: Use when a plant contains a compressor: gas compression by pressure ratio and isentropic efficiency, with surge and discharge-temperature limits.
- condenser: Use when a plant contains a condenser: a hot working fluid condenses into a cooling-water stream whose temperature rise sets the duty and approach.
- dc-load: Use when a plant contains a dc_load: the IT electrical demand, the fraction of its heat sent to coolant and the required coolant return temperature.
- district-heat: Use when a plant supplies district heat through an exhaust heat exchanger flagged useful or a heat pump lifting chiller rejection heat to the network.
- electric-chiller: Use when a plant contains an electric_chiller: vapour-compression cooling whose part-load COP depends on temperatures, approach and fouling.
- evaporator: Use when exhaust boils a working fluid in an orc_evaporator: bubble-point pinch, superheat, flow position, dryout and freeze limits.
- gas-engine: Use when a plant contains a gas_engine component: a reciprocating gas engine sized by rated electrical output, with air, fuel and exhaust ports.
- heat-pump: Use when a plant contains a heat_pump: heat lifted from a source stream to a hotter sink, limited by Lorenz COP, sink temperature, approach and lift.
- heat-pump-district-heat: Use when a plant delivers district heat, with a heat_pump on the chiller heat-rejection loop or a heat exchanger flagged useful_heat on the exhaust.
- heat-rejector: Use when a plant contains a heat_rejector (dry cooler or evaporative cooling tower) closing a cooling-water loop.
- hrsg: Use when a plant contains an hrsg: exhaust heats feedwater to steam at a set steam pressure, limited by the economiser approach, pinch and stack temperature.
- orc: Use when a plant has an organic Rankine cycle: an orc_evaporator and orc_turbine on exhaust heat, with fluid limits, pinch, flow position and a dry or wet expansion.
- orc-bottoming: Use when a plant contains an organic Rankine cycle (orc_evaporator, orc_turbine, pump, condenser) on exhaust heat.
- pump: Use when a plant contains a pump: liquid pressurisation by outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with NPSH, cavitation and two-phase-inlet limits.
- recuperator: Use when a plant contains a recuperator: two streams exchange heat to a set cold outlet with pressure drops, a minimum approach and an optional delivered-heat flag.
- turbine: Use when a plant contains a turbine: gas or steam expansion through an outlet pressure and isentropic efficiency, with backpressure and blade-temperature limits.

prompt.content:
You design on-site energy plants for AI data centres. Given a site, choose the plant configuration and set its parameters. The plant must solve, pass the physics checks (mass and energy balance, exergy closure, no negative exergy destruction, no temperature cross, plausible ranges) and meet the site: its IT electricity with no grid import, its chilled-water load, and any water limit. Among valid plants, the one that burns the least fuel wins. Answer with a short <rationale> that cites only quantities you expect the solved plant to show (MW, K), then a <design> block with one `key = value` per line and exactly the keys your choices require. Catalog: prime_mover in {turbine, engine}; cooling in {absorption, electric}; rejection in {dry, wet}; bottoming in {none, orc_r245fa, orc_cyclopentane, orc_toluene}; dT_rej in [5, 12]; PR in [10, 30]; T4 in [1300, 1600]; T_hw in [353.15, 383.15]; dT_hw in [5, 20]; P_orc_bar in [10, 25]; orc_frac in [0.1, 1]. PR and T4 apply only to a turbine; T_hw and dT_hw only to absorption cooling; P_orc_bar and orc_frac only when bottoming is an ORC (orc_frac 0.1 = smallest working-fluid flow, 1.0 = largest). If the site has a heat demand, also set heat_source = exhaust or heat_pump.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks (compact)
Simulated plants for AI data centres; a solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so cite only numbers the solver reproduces.
Conventions: SI units (K, Pa, W, kg/s); eps/dp/PR are fractions, never percent; temperature in K, never degC. Plant graph: `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream; endpoints are `<comp>.<port>` or `ext:<name>`. Gas fluids are CGAM_AIR/FLUE/CH4; others are CoolProp liquids (Water, R245fa, Cyclopentane, Toluene); a port accepts only its fluid class. A `fixed` stream produced by a component is a tear closing a loop: change both sides together. Flows a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air/fuel, chiller gen/rejection, IT coolant, heat-pump sink).
Answer format (design): <rationale> then <design> with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.

SKILL CATALOG (descriptions only; full text arrives as a tool result):
Primary skill for design: design-catalog: Use for Design tasks: choosing prime mover, cooling, heat rejection, bottoming cycle and district-heat source for a site.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks

You work on simulated plants for AI data centres (gas prime mover, cooling, heat recovery). A solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so only claims that the solver would reproduce are useful.

## Conventions
- SI units: K, Pa, W, kg/s. Efficiencies, second-law fractions (`eps`) and pressure-drop fractions (`dp*`) are fractions, never percent. Temperatures are kelvin, never degrees Celsius.
- A plant is a graph. `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream. Endpoints are `<component>.<port>` or `ext:<name>` (a boundary).
- Fluid classes: gas streams are `CGAM_AIR`, `FLUE`, `CH4`; every other fluid is a liquid or two-phase CoolProp fluid (`Water`, `R245fa`, `Cyclopentane`, `Toluene`). A port accepts only its own class.
- A stream whose source is a component but which carries `fixed` values is a tear stream: it closes a loop, and its fixed T and P must equal what the producing component computes. Never change one side of a tear without the other.
- Flows that a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air and fuel, chiller generator and rejection flows, IT coolant flow, heat-pump sink flow).

## What the verifiers check
V1 mass balance, V2 energy balance, V3 exergy: closure and no negative exergy destruction in any component, V4 no temperature cross (min approach below 0 K fails), V5 second-law and Carnot bounds, V6 unit and range checks, V7 numbers in your text must match the solver, V8 site requirements (IT load served, no grid import unless allowed, cooling, heat, water limit).

## Reading a solver error
- E_PROP_RANGE: a value is non-positive, a unit slip, or outside the property data (a pressure of 20 Pa, a temperature of 1226 K entered as 1226 degC).
- E_TEMP_CROSS: heat cannot flow as specified: hot and cold inlets swapped, a duty larger than the hot stream can supply, or an inlet colder than the achievable outlet.
- E_NOT_CONVERGED: a tear stream does not close, or an outlet temperature is not reachable.
- E_FLUID_MISMATCH: a stream's fluid class does not fit the port it feeds.
- E_DISCONNECTED, E_OVER_SPECIFIED, E_UNDER_SPECIFIED: a port has no stream or two, or a value that should be solved is given, or one is missing.
- Solved but failing a check: read the check name and its detail; V6 names the offending parameter.

## Answer formats
- Repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown, then `<edits>` with lines `SET <component>.<param> = <number>`, `SET @<stream>.<field> = <number>`, `REWIRE @<stream>.<to|from> = <component>.<port>`, `FLUID @<stream> = <fluid>`. Change as little as possible; you cannot add or remove components.
- Design: `<rationale>` then `<design>` with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.
- Audit: `<analysis>`, `<ranking>A > B > C</ranking>`, `<change>SET ...</change>`, `<prediction>fuel_change_mw = ...</prediction>`.
- Ledger repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown (MW), then `<fix>` with lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

## Habits
1. Find which stream or parameter the error or failing check points at before editing anything.
2. Prefer the explanation that fixes the reported failure with the fewest edits.
3. Never invent numbers: quote what the input shows, or say what you expect the solved plant to show.

# Design catalog

Objective: among plants that solve, pass all checks and meet the site, burn the least fuel. Mechanisms below hold at the default technology constants of these plants (engine electrical efficiency 0.43, chiller COP cap 0.8); they are not laws.

- Prime mover: an engine converts more fuel to electricity, but only its exhaust is recovered. A turbine has hotter, larger exhaust and can drive absorption cooling for a larger chilled share. If the chilled load is too large for engine exhaust, the exhaust heat exchanger fails (temperature cross).
- Cooling: absorption cooling uses exhaust heat and adds no electrical load; electric cooling adds parasitic electricity, so a larger prime mover. Absorption needs enough exhaust heat at a high enough temperature.
- Rejection: a wet tower rejects at wet-bulb plus 5 K, a dry cooler at dry-bulb plus 8 K. Hot, dry climates hurt dry coolers most (lower chiller COP, possible temperature cross). A site water limit rules out wet towers.
- Bottoming cycle: an ORC makes electricity from exhaust that is left after other recoveries, so it lowers fuel. Exhaust above the fluid's vapour limit cannot be used (about 850 K turbine exhaust is too hot for all three fluids here); choose the fluid whose limit fits the exhaust temperature after upstream recovery.
- District heat: exhaust heat is free if enough remains after cooling; a heat pump costs electricity but leaves exhaust for an ORC.
- Continuous parameters: turbine PR and T4 trade cycle efficiency against exhaust temperature; hot-water `T_hw` and `dT_hw` must keep the generator duty feasible; `dT_rej` sets rejection flow and temperature level; `P_orc_bar` and `orc_frac` must keep the pinch and the exhaust floor feasible.
- Check the feasibility mechanisms (exhaust heat available vs duty, temperature levels, water) before optimising fuel.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks

You work on simulated plants for AI data centres (gas prime mover, cooling, heat recovery). A solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so only claims that the solver would reproduce are useful.

## Conventions
- SI units: K, Pa, W, kg/s. Efficiencies, second-law fractions (`eps`) and pressure-drop fractions (`dp*`) are fractions, never percent. Temperatures are kelvin, never degrees Celsius.
- A plant is a graph. `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream. Endpoints are `<component>.<port>` or `ext:<name>` (a boundary).
- Fluid classes: gas streams are `CGAM_AIR`, `FLUE`, `CH4`; every other fluid is a liquid or two-phase CoolProp fluid (`Water`, `R245fa`, `Cyclopentane`, `Toluene`). A port accepts only its own class.
- A stream whose source is a component but which carries `fixed` values is a tear stream: it closes a loop, and its fixed T and P must equal what the producing component computes. Never change one side of a tear without the other.
- Flows that a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air and fuel, chiller generator and rejection flows, IT coolant flow, heat-pump sink flow).

## What the verifiers check
V1 mass balance, V2 energy balance, V3 exergy: closure and no negative exergy destruction in any component, V4 no temperature cross (min approach below 0 K fails), V5 second-law and Carnot bounds, V6 unit and range checks, V7 numbers in your text must match the solver, V8 site requirements (IT load served, no grid import unless allowed, cooling, heat, water limit).

## Reading a solver error
- E_PROP_RANGE: a value is non-positive, a unit slip, or outside the property data (a pressure of 20 Pa, a temperature of 1226 K entered as 1226 degC).
- E_TEMP_CROSS: heat cannot flow as specified: hot and cold inlets swapped, a duty larger than the hot stream can supply, or an inlet colder than the achievable outlet.
- E_NOT_CONVERGED: a tear stream does not close, or an outlet temperature is not reachable.
- E_FLUID_MISMATCH: a stream's fluid class does not fit the port it feeds.
- E_DISCONNECTED, E_OVER_SPECIFIED, E_UNDER_SPECIFIED: a port has no stream or two, or a value that should be solved is given, or one is missing.
- Solved but failing a check: read the check name and its detail; V6 names the offending parameter.

## Answer formats
- Repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown, then `<edits>` with lines `SET <component>.<param> = <number>`, `SET @<stream>.<field> = <number>`, `REWIRE @<stream>.<to|from> = <component>.<port>`, `FLUID @<stream> = <fluid>`. Change as little as possible; you cannot add or remove components.
- Design: `<rationale>` then `<design>` with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.
- Audit: `<analysis>`, `<ranking>A > B > C</ranking>`, `<change>SET ...</change>`, `<prediction>fuel_change_mw = ...</prediction>`.
- Ledger repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown (MW), then `<fix>` with lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

## Habits
1. Find which stream or parameter the error or failing check points at before editing anything.
2. Prefer the explanation that fixes the reported failure with the fewest edits.
3. Never invent numbers: quote what the input shows, or say what you expect the solved plant to show.

# Design catalog

Objective: among plants that solve, pass all checks and meet the site, burn the least fuel. Mechanisms below hold at the default technology constants of these plants (engine electrical efficiency 0.43, chiller COP cap 0.8); they are not laws.

- Prime mover: an engine converts more fuel to electricity, but only its exhaust is recovered. A turbine has hotter, larger exhaust and can drive absorption cooling for a larger chilled share. If the chilled load is too large for engine exhaust, the exhaust heat exchanger fails (temperature cross).
- Cooling: absorption cooling uses exhaust heat and adds no electrical load; electric cooling adds parasitic electricity, so a larger prime mover. Absorption needs enough exhaust heat at a high enough temperature.
- Rejection: a wet tower rejects at wet-bulb plus 5 K, a dry cooler at dry-bulb plus 8 K. Hot, dry climates hurt dry coolers most (lower chiller COP, possible temperature cross). A site water limit rules out wet towers.
- Bottoming cycle: an ORC makes electricity from exhaust that is left after other recoveries, so it lowers fuel. Exhaust above the fluid's vapour limit cannot be used (about 850 K turbine exhaust is too hot for all three fluids here); choose the fluid whose limit fits the exhaust temperature after upstream recovery.
- District heat: exhaust heat is free if enough remains after cooling; a heat pump costs electricity but leaves exhaust for an ORC.
- Continuous parameters: turbine PR and T4 trade cycle efficiency against exhaust temperature; hot-water `T_hw` and `dT_hw` must keep the generator duty feasible; `dT_rej` sets rejection flow and temperature level; `P_orc_bar` and `orc_frac` must keep the pinch and the exhaust floor feasible.
- Check the feasibility mechanisms (exhaust heat available vs duty, temperature levels, water) before optimising fuel.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks

You work on simulated plants for AI data centres (gas prime mover, cooling, heat recovery). A solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so only claims that the solver would reproduce are useful.

## Conventions
- SI units: K, Pa, W, kg/s. Efficiencies, second-law fractions (`eps`) and pressure-drop fractions (`dp*`) are fractions, never percent. Temperatures are kelvin, never degrees Celsius.
- A plant is a graph. `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream. Endpoints are `<component>.<port>` or `ext:<name>` (a boundary).
- Fluid classes: gas streams are `CGAM_AIR`, `FLUE`, `CH4`; every other fluid is a liquid or two-phase CoolProp fluid (`Water`, `R245fa`, `Cyclopentane`, `Toluene`). A port accepts only its own class.
- A stream whose source is a component but which carries `fixed` values is a tear stream: it closes a loop, and its fixed T and P must equal what the producing component computes. Never change one side of a tear without the other.
- Flows that a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air and fuel, chiller generator and rejection flows, IT coolant flow, heat-pump sink flow).

## What the verifiers check
V1 mass balance, V2 energy balance, V3 exergy: closure and no negative exergy destruction in any component, V4 no temperature cross (min approach below 0 K fails), V5 second-law and Carnot bounds, V6 unit and range checks, V7 numbers in your text must match the solver, V8 site requirements (IT load served, no grid import unless allowed, cooling, heat, water limit).

## Reading a solver error
- E_PROP_RANGE: a value is non-positive, a unit slip, or outside the property data (a pressure of 20 Pa, a temperature of 1226 K entered as 1226 degC).
- E_TEMP_CROSS: heat cannot flow as specified: hot and cold inlets swapped, a duty larger than the hot stream can supply, or an inlet colder than the achievable outlet.
- E_NOT_CONVERGED: a tear stream does not close, or an outlet temperature is not reachable.
- E_FLUID_MISMATCH: a stream's fluid class does not fit the port it feeds.
- E_DISCONNECTED, E_OVER_SPECIFIED, E_UNDER_SPECIFIED: a port has no stream or two, or a value that should be solved is given, or one is missing.
- Solved but failing a check: read the check name and its detail; V6 names the offending parameter.

## Answer formats
- Repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown, then `<edits>` with lines `SET <component>.<param> = <number>`, `SET @<stream>.<field> = <number>`, `REWIRE @<stream>.<to|from> = <component>.<port>`, `FLUID @<stream> = <fluid>`. Change as little as possible; you cannot add or remove components.
- Design: `<rationale>` then `<design>` with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.
- Audit: `<analysis>`, `<ranking>A > B > C</ranking>`, `<change>SET ...</change>`, `<prediction>fuel_change_mw = ...</prediction>`.
- Ledger repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown (MW), then `<fix>` with lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

## Habits
1. Find which stream or parameter the error or failing check points at before editing anything.
2. Prefer the explanation that fixes the reported failure with the fewest edits.
3. Never invent numbers: quote what the input shows, or say what you expect the solved plant to show.

# Design catalog

Objective: among plants that solve, pass all checks and meet the site, burn the least fuel. Mechanisms below hold at the default technology constants of these plants (engine electrical efficiency 0.43, chiller COP cap 0.8); they are not laws.

- Prime mover: an engine converts more fuel to electricity, but only its exhaust is recovered. A turbine has hotter, larger exhaust and can drive absorption cooling for a larger chilled share. If the chilled load is too large for engine exhaust, the exhaust heat exchanger fails (temperature cross).
- Cooling: absorption cooling uses exhaust heat and adds no electrical load; electric cooling adds parasitic electricity, so a larger prime mover. Absorption needs enough exhaust heat at a high enough temperature.
- Rejection: a wet tower rejects at wet-bulb plus 5 K, a dry cooler at dry-bulb plus 8 K. Hot, dry climates hurt dry coolers most (lower chiller COP, possible temperature cross). A site water limit rules out wet towers.
- Bottoming cycle: an ORC makes electricity from exhaust that is left after other recoveries, so it lowers fuel. Exhaust above the fluid's vapour limit cannot be used (about 850 K turbine exhaust is too hot for all three fluids here); choose the fluid whose limit fits the exhaust temperature after upstream recovery.
- District heat: exhaust heat is free if enough remains after cooling; a heat pump costs electricity but leaves exhaust for an ORC.
- Continuous parameters: turbine PR and T4 trade cycle efficiency against exhaust temperature; hot-water `T_hw` and `dT_hw` must keep the generator duty feasible; `dT_rej` sets rejection flow and temperature level; `P_orc_bar` and `orc_frac` must keep the pinch and the exhaust floor feasible.
- Check the feasibility mechanisms (exhaust heat available vs duty, temperature levels, water) before optimising fuel.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks

You work on simulated plants for AI data centres (gas prime mover, cooling, heat recovery). A solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so only claims that the solver would reproduce are useful.

## Conventions
- SI units: K, Pa, W, kg/s. Efficiencies, second-law fractions (`eps`) and pressure-drop fractions (`dp*`) are fractions, never percent. Temperatures are kelvin, never degrees Celsius.
- A plant is a graph. `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream. Endpoints are `<component>.<port>` or `ext:<name>` (a boundary).
- Fluid classes: gas streams are `CGAM_AIR`, `FLUE`, `CH4`; every other fluid is a liquid or two-phase CoolProp fluid (`Water`, `R245fa`, `Cyclopentane`, `Toluene`). A port accepts only its own class.
- A stream whose source is a component but which carries `fixed` values is a tear stream: it closes a loop, and its fixed T and P must equal what the producing component computes. Never change one side of a tear without the other.
- Flows that a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air and fuel, chiller generator and rejection flows, IT coolant flow, heat-pump sink flow).

## What the verifiers check
V1 mass balance, V2 energy balance, V3 exergy: closure and no negative exergy destruction in any component, V4 no temperature cross (min approach below 0 K fails), V5 second-law and Carnot bounds, V6 unit and range checks, V7 numbers in your text must match the solver, V8 site requirements (IT load served, no grid import unless allowed, cooling, heat, water limit).

## Reading a solver error
- E_PROP_RANGE: a value is non-positive, a unit slip, or outside the property data (a pressure of 20 Pa, a temperature of 1226 K entered as 1226 degC).
- E_TEMP_CROSS: heat cannot flow as specified: hot and cold inlets swapped, a duty larger than the hot stream can supply, or an inlet colder than the achievable outlet.
- E_NOT_CONVERGED: a tear stream does not close, or an outlet temperature is not reachable.
- E_FLUID_MISMATCH: a stream's fluid class does not fit the port it feeds.
- E_DISCONNECTED, E_OVER_SPECIFIED, E_UNDER_SPECIFIED: a port has no stream or two, or a value that should be solved is given, or one is missing.
- Solved but failing a check: read the check name and its detail; V6 names the offending parameter.

## Answer formats
- Repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown, then `<edits>` with lines `SET <component>.<param> = <number>`, `SET @<stream>.<field> = <number>`, `REWIRE @<stream>.<to|from> = <component>.<port>`, `FLUID @<stream> = <fluid>`. Change as little as possible; you cannot add or remove components.
- Design: `<rationale>` then `<design>` with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.
- Audit: `<analysis>`, `<ranking>A > B > C</ranking>`, `<change>SET ...</change>`, `<prediction>fuel_change_mw = ...</prediction>`.
- Ledger repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown (MW), then `<fix>` with lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

## Habits
1. Find which stream or parameter the error or failing check points at before editing anything.
2. Prefer the explanation that fixes the reported failure with the fewest edits.
3. Never invent numbers: quote what the input shows, or say what you expect the solved plant to show.

## Components
<!-- AUTO:all -->
- `compressor`: ports in, out; params PR, eta_s
- `turbine`: ports in, out; params P_out, eta_s
- `orc_turbine`: ports in, out; params P_out, eta_s
- `pump`: ports in, out; params P_out, eta_s
- `combustor`: ports air_in, fuel_in, out; params T_out, dp, q_loss
- `recuperator`: ports cold_in, cold_out, hot_in, hot_out; params T_cold_out, dp_cold, dp_hot, useful_heat
- `hrsg`: ports hot_in, hot_out, water_in, steam_out; params P_steam, dp_gas, econ_approach_K
- `orc_evaporator`: ports hot_in, hot_out, cold_in, cold_out; params pinch_K, dp_hot, flow_frac, T_stack_min, T_max_K
- `condenser`: ports hot_in, hot_out, cold_in, cold_out; params dT_cw
- `dc_load`: ports in, out; params P_it, chilled_fraction, T_return
- `absorption_chiller`: ports gen_in, gen_out, evap_in, evap_out, rej_in, rej_out; params T_chw_out, T_gen_out, dT_rej, eps, COP_max
- `heat_pump`: ports src_in, src_out, sink_in, sink_out; params T_sink_out, eps, approach_K, Q_sink, dT_src
- `electric_chiller`: ports evap_in, evap_out, rej_in, rej_out; params T_chw_out, dT_rej, eps, approach_K
- `heat_rejector`: ports in, out; params kind, approach_K, fan_frac

SKILL design-catalog: Use for Design tasks: choosing prime mover, cooling, heat rejection, bottoming cycle and district-heat source for a site.
# Design catalog

Objective: among plants that solve, pass all checks and meet the site, burn the least fuel. Mechanisms below hold at the default technology constants of these plants (engine electrical efficiency 0.43, chiller COP cap 0.8); they are not laws.

- Prime mover: an engine converts more fuel to electricity, but only its exhaust is recovered. A turbine has hotter, larger exhaust and can drive absorption cooling for a larger chilled share. If the chilled load is too large for engine exhaust, the exhaust heat exchanger fails (temperature cross).
- Cooling: absorption cooling uses exhaust heat and adds no electrical load; electric cooling adds parasitic electricity, so a larger prime mover. Absorption needs enough exhaust heat at a high enough temperature.
- Rejection: a wet tower rejects at wet-bulb plus 5 K, a dry cooler at dry-bulb plus 8 K. Hot, dry climates hurt dry coolers most (lower chiller COP, possible temperature cross). A site water limit rules out wet towers.
- Bottoming cycle: an ORC makes electricity from exhaust that is left after other recoveries, so it lowers fuel. Exhaust above the fluid's vapour limit cannot be used (about 850 K turbine exhaust is too hot for all three fluids here); choose the fluid whose limit fits the exhaust temperature after upstream recovery.
- District heat: exhaust heat is free if enough remains after cooling; a heat pump costs electricity but leaves exhaust for an ORC.
- Continuous parameters: turbine PR and T4 trade cycle efficiency against exhaust temperature; hot-water `T_hw` and `dT_hw` must keep the generator duty feasible; `dT_rej` sets rejection flow and temperature level; `P_orc_bar` and `orc_frac` must keep the pinch and the exhaust floor feasible.
- Check the feasibility mechanisms (exhaust heat available vs duty, temperature levels, water) before optimising fuel.

A dry rejection system is used to comply with the zero-water limit. The turbine parameters (PR=18, T4=1450 K) are balanced to provide enough exhaust temperature for the absorption generator while maintaining high electrical efficiency. The absorption chiller is configured with T_hw=375 K and dT_hw=15 K to ensure the generator duty is met without temperature cross.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks

You work on simulated plants for AI data centres (gas prime mover, cooling, heat recovery). A solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so only claims that the solver would reproduce are useful.

## Conventions
- SI units: K, Pa, W, kg/s. Efficiencies, second-law fractions (`eps`) and pressure-drop fractions (`dp*`) are fractions, never percent. Temperatures are kelvin, never degrees Celsius.
- A plant is a graph. `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream. Endpoints are `<component>.<port>` or `ext:<name>` (a boundary).
- Fluid classes: gas streams are `CGAM_AIR`, `FLUE`, `CH4`; every other fluid is a liquid or two-phase CoolProp fluid (`Water`, `R245fa`, `Cyclopentane`, `Toluene`). A port accepts only its own class.
- A stream whose source is a component but which carries `fixed` values is a tear stream: it closes a loop, and its fixed T and P must equal what the producing component computes. Never change one side of a tear without the other.
- Flows that a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air and fuel, chiller generator and rejection flows, IT coolant flow, heat-pump sink flow).

## What the verifiers check
V1 mass balance, V2 energy balance, V3 exergy: closure and no negative exergy destruction in any component, V4 no temperature cross (min approach below 0 K fails), V5 second-law and Carnot bounds, V6 unit and range checks, V7 numbers in your text must match the solver, V8 site requirements (IT load served, no grid import unless allowed, cooling, heat, water limit).

## Reading a solver error
- E_PROP_RANGE: a value is non-positive, a unit slip, or outside the property data (a pressure of 20 Pa, a temperature of 1226 K entered as 1226 degC).
- E_TEMP_CROSS: heat cannot flow as specified: hot and cold inlets swapped, a duty larger than the hot stream can supply, or an inlet colder than the achievable outlet.
- E_NOT_CONVERGED: a tear stream does not close, or an outlet temperature is not reachable.
- E_FLUID_MISMATCH: a stream's fluid class does not fit the port it feeds.
- E_DISCONNECTED, E_OVER_SPECIFIED, E_UNDER_SPECIFIED: a port has no stream or two, or a value that should be solved is given, or one is missing.
- Solved but failing a check: read the check name and its detail; V6 names the offending parameter.

## Answer formats
- Repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown, then `<edits>` with lines `SET <component>.<param> = <number>`, `SET @<stream>.<field> = <number>`, `REWIRE @<stream>.<to|from> = <component>.<port>`, `FLUID @<stream> = <fluid>`. Change as little as possible; you cannot add or remove components.
- Design: `<rationale>` then `<design>` with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.
- Audit: `<analysis>`, `<ranking>A > B > C</ranking>`, `<change>SET ...</change>`, `<prediction>fuel_change_mw = ...</prediction>`.
- Ledger repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown (MW), then `<fix>` with lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

## Habits
1. Find which stream or parameter the error or failing check points at before editing anything.
2. Prefer the explanation that fixes the reported failure with the fewest edits.
3. Never invent numbers: quote what the input shows, or say what you expect the solved plant to show.

# Design catalog

Objective: among plants that solve, pass all checks and meet the site, burn the least fuel. Mechanisms below hold at the default technology constants of these plants (engine electrical efficiency 0.43, chiller COP cap 0.8); they are not laws.

- Prime mover: an engine converts more fuel to electricity, but only its exhaust is recovered. A turbine has hotter, larger exhaust and can drive absorption cooling for a larger chilled share. If the chilled load is too large for engine exhaust, the exhaust heat exchanger fails (temperature cross).
- Cooling: absorption cooling uses exhaust heat and adds no electrical load; electric cooling adds parasitic electricity, so a larger prime mover. Absorption needs enough exhaust heat at a high enough temperature.
- Rejection: a wet tower rejects at wet-bulb plus 5 K, a dry cooler at dry-bulb plus 8 K. Hot, dry climates hurt dry coolers most (lower chiller COP, possible temperature cross). A site water limit rules out wet towers.
- Bottoming cycle: an ORC makes electricity from exhaust that is left after other recoveries, so it lowers fuel. Exhaust above the fluid's vapour limit cannot be used (about 850 K turbine exhaust is too hot for all three fluids here); choose the fluid whose limit fits the exhaust temperature after upstream recovery.
- District heat: exhaust heat is free if enough remains after cooling; a heat pump costs electricity but leaves exhaust for an ORC.
- Continuous parameters: turbine PR and T4 trade cycle efficiency against exhaust temperature; hot-water `T_hw` and `dT_hw` must keep the generator duty feasible; `dT_rej` sets rejection flow and temperature level; `P_orc_bar` and `orc_frac` must keep the pinch and the exhaust floor feasible.
- Check the feasibility mechanisms (exhaust heat available vs duty, temperature levels, water) before optimising fuel.

# AGENTS.md: energy-plant tasks

You work on simulated plants for AI data centres (gas prime mover, cooling, heat recovery). A solver and physics verifiers judge every answer, so only claims that the solver would reproduce are useful.

## Conventions
- SI units: K, Pa, W, kg/s. Efficiencies, second-law fractions (`eps`) and pressure-drop fractions (`dp*`) are fractions, never percent. Temperatures are kelvin, never degrees Celsius.
- A plant is a graph. `C <id> <type> {params}` is a component; `S <id> <from> -> <to> <fluid> {extras}` is a stream. Endpoints are `<component>.<port>` or `ext:<name>` (a boundary).
- Fluid classes: gas streams are `CGAM_AIR`, `FLUE`, `CH4`; every other fluid is a liquid or two-phase CoolProp fluid (`Water`, `R245fa`, `Cyclopentane`, `Toluene`). A port accepts only its own class.
- A stream whose source is a component but which carries `fixed` values is a tear stream: it closes a loop, and its fixed T and P must equal what the producing component computes. Never change one side of a tear without the other.
- Flows that a component solves itself must not be specified (engine air and fuel, chiller generator and rejection flows, IT coolant flow, heat-pump sink flow).

## What the verifiers check
V1 mass balance, V2 energy balance, V3 exergy: closure and no negative exergy destruction in any component, V4 no temperature cross (min approach below 0 K fails), V5 second-law and Carnot bounds, V6 unit and range checks, V7 numbers in your text must match the solver, V8 site requirements (IT load served, no grid import unless allowed, cooling, heat, water limit).

## Reading a solver error
- E_PROP_RANGE: a value is non-positive, a unit slip, or outside the property data (a pressure of 20 Pa, a temperature of 1226 K entered as 1226 degC).
- E_TEMP_CROSS: heat cannot flow as specified: hot and cold inlets swapped, a duty larger than the hot stream can supply, or an inlet colder than the achievable outlet.
- E_NOT_CONVERGED: a tear stream does not close, or an outlet temperature is not reachable.
- E_FLUID_MISMATCH: a stream's fluid class does not fit the port it feeds.
- E_DISCONNECTED, E_OVER_SPECIFIED, E_UNDER_SPECIFIED: a port has no stream or two, or a value that should be solved is given, or one is missing.
- Solved but failing a check: read the check name and its detail; V6 names the offending parameter.

## Answer formats
- Repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown, then `<edits>` with lines `SET <component>.<param> = <number>`, `SET @<stream>.<field> = <number>`, `REWIRE @<stream>.<to|from> = <component>.<port>`, `FLUID @<stream> = <fluid>`. Change as little as possible; you cannot add or remove components.
- Design: `<rationale>` then `<design>` with `key = value` lines, exactly the keys your choices require.
- Audit: `<analysis>`, `<ranking>A > B > C</ranking>`, `<change>SET ...</change>`, `<prediction>fuel_change_mw = ...</prediction>`.
- Ledger repair: `<diagnosis>` citing only numbers shown (MW), then `<fix>` with lines `FIX T0 = <expr>`, `FIX E[<stream>] = <expr>`, `FIX ED[<component>] = <expr>`.

## Habits
1. Find which stream or parameter the error or failing check points at before editing anything.
2. Prefer the explanation that fixes the reported failure with the fewest edits.
3. Never invent numbers: quote what the input shows, or say what you expect the solved plant to show.

# Design catalog

Objective: among plants that solve, pass all checks and meet the site, burn the least fuel. Mechanisms below hold at the default technology constants of these plants (engine electrical efficiency 0.43, chiller COP cap 0.8); they are not laws.

- Prime mover: an engine converts more fuel to electricity, but only its exhaust is recovered. A turbine has hotter, larger exhaust and can drive absorption cooling for a larger chilled share. If the chilled load is too large for engine exhaust, the exhaust heat exchanger fails (temperature cross).
- Cooling: absorption cooling uses exhaust heat and adds no electrical load; electric cooling adds parasitic electricity, so a larger prime mover. Absorption needs enough exhaust heat at a high enough temperature.
- Rejection: a wet tower rejects at wet-bulb plus 5 K, a dry cooler at dry-bulb plus 8 K. Hot, dry climates hurt dry coolers most (lower chiller COP, possible temperature cross). A site water limit rules out wet towers.
- Bottoming cycle: an ORC makes electricity from exhaust that is left after other recoveries, so it lowers fuel. Exhaust above the fluid's vapour limit cannot be used (about 850 K turbine exhaust is too hot for all three fluids here); choose the fluid whose limit fits the exhaust temperature after upstream recovery.
- District heat: exhaust heat is free if enough remains after cooling; a heat pump costs electricity but leaves exhaust for an ORC.
- Continuous parameters: turbine PR and T4 trade cycle efficiency against exhaust temperature; hot-water `T_hw` and `dT_hw` must keep the generator duty feasible; `dT_rej` sets rejection flow and temperature level; `P_orc_bar` and `orc_frac` must keep the pinch and the exhaust floor feasible.
- Check the feasibility mechanisms (exhaust heat available vs duty, temperature levels, water) before optimising fuel.
